q1_issues.issue: 'many' is slotted as the property of a ConditionalProperty, but the instruction set routes quantity/proportion words to strength, or to CardinalityPhrase when the phrase counts things, never to a property symbol — and no individual party can hold the property 'many', which is what the seeded cond_prop distribution would hand it.
The existential 'there are ... parties' mints no witness or group, so nothing in the parse asserts that any parties exist.
'around' is dropped and a temporal restriction is placed in the condition slot, which the instruction set licenses only for a locative or domain PP restricting a kind-level claim.
The QuantifierPhrase companion's second slot holds 'many' rather than a predicate or verb lemma, inheriting the same mis-slotting.

q2_gaps: habitual / generic existential 'there are often N Xs around T' — the frequency-adverb rule assumes a generic statement or an event rule, and a bare existential supplies no eventuality for Every / TimesPer / Time to attach to
'around <named time>' — an approximation hedge on a non-clock, named time (the distribution form is defined only for clock times and measures)
notes: The 0.8 strength for 'often' and the Name atom for the proper noun Midsummer are each correct in themselves; the defect is the structure they are attached to.
